meaning:
1) to bar, lock, bolt
1a) (Qal) to bar, lock, bolt

elsewhere.note: Then Ehud went out onto the porch, and shut the doors of the upper room on him, and locked them.
Then he called his servant who ministered to him, and said, “Now put this woman out from me, and bolt the door after her.”
The men who have been mentioned by name rose up and took the captives, and with the plunder clothed all who were naked among them, dressed them, gave them…
My sister, my bride, is a locked up garden; a locked up spring, a sealed fountain.
I clothed you also with embroidered work, and put sealskin sandals on you. I dressed you with fine linen and covered you with silk.
